title: Lattice Yang-Mills theory: spacing-uniform obstructions, the mass gap up to the Dobrushin ceiling and in a forest gauge, and Lean certificate
description: Three RevTeX papers and a Lean 4/Mathlib certificate. (1) Spacing-Uniform Lattice Inequalities Cannot Produce the Yang-Mills Mass Gap: a lattice gap uniform in lattice units forces vanishing continuum two-point functions; volume, cumulant, Bianchi, running-coupling and curvature obstructions; the open residual (Hypothesis R). (2) Mass Gap of Lattice Yang-Mills Theory up to the Dobrushin Ceiling: the sharp Hessian bound 4d, uniqueness and a lattice mass gap for |beta|<1/(8d), the sharp quarter W1(nu_b,nu_b') <= |b-b'|/4 for von Mises-Fisher laws on the three-sphere, and hence uniqueness and a lattice mass gap m >= -log(9 beta_W/2) for four-dimensional SU(2) up to beta_W = 2/9, the ceiling of all single-link Dobrushin arguments; a gauge-invariant finite-box criterion. (3) Mass Gap of Four-Dimensional Lattice Yang-Mills Theory in a Forest Gauge: a field of straight lines meeting every plaquette in exactly one link, so that each free link has twelve partners; a unique free-boundary state, reflection positivity, decay and a transfer-matrix gap m >= -log(3 beta_W) for SU(2) up to beta_W = 1/3, the ceiling of single-link Dobrushin after any forest gauge fixing; a gauge-fixed Hessian bound 29/2 for every SU(N) and SO(N); and for SU(3) a gap m >= -log(1.4218 beta_W) for beta_W <= 45/64, from a spectral-gap bound for the one-link measure and a cover of the staple sums by 865 boxes certified in ball arithmetic. The continuum Yang-Mills existence and mass-gap problem remains open. Lean: 70 theorems and lemmas, no sorry, standard axioms only.
